name: cache-coverage
title: Cache Coverage: All LLM Paths
prompt:
Do these tasks in order:

1. EXPLORE: Use an explore agent to find the current population of Japan (a single number).

2. SIAS (Super-Intelligent Autonomous System): Spawn a sub-agent to do this multi-step task:
   a. Use a browser agent to visit https://www.random.org/integers/?num=1&min=1&max=100&col=1&base=10&format=plain and return the number shown on the page.
   b. Use Claude Code to run this Python script and return the output: import random; random.seed(42); print(random.randint(1, 100))
   c. Multiply the two numbers (browser result × code result) and return the product.

3. MULTIPLY: Take the population of Japan from step 1 and multiply it by the product from step 2.

4. MESSAGE: Send an email to andy@roselabs.ai with the subject 'Cache Benchmark Result' containing the final number from step 3.
eval_prompt: Agent used all required tool paths: explore agent (population lookup), SIAS sub-agent (which internally used browser agent and Claude Code), reasoning/multiplication, and message_person (email to andy@roselabs.ai). An approval was triggered for the message. Each tool type was used exactly once.

eval_prompt: Agent received the image attachment, processed it (likely via Claude Code or browser agent), and produced a red-tinted version of the original image. A file_pointer output with an image is present in the messages.

name: files-in-sub-agents

name: family-office-angel-outreach
title: Family Office & Angel Outreach
prompt:
I've attached a CSV of ~700 angels. Get me on a call to chat with as many of the people on this list as possible.

Each message should be personalized, sent from andy@roselabs.ai and be centered around getting feedback about ML research I'm doing in mass agent networks. Here is the blog post I wrote: https://www.roselabs.ai/research/task-decomposer

We need to make sure we run this process with world class persistence, etiquette, and attention to detail. I want to have one sub agent manage each individual relationship, and be responsible for follow-ups, responses, getting them on a call via generating a calendly link on a browser agent etc.

Since you are limited on the sub-agents you can create, you may need to split the file up into chunks which are handed off to each agent which recursively reduce the list down to one agent per person. Chunk it as you see fit.
eval_prompt: Agent read the CSV attachment of ~700 angels, spawned sub-agents to research and manage outreach per person or chunk, and called message_person to send personalized emails from andy@roselabs.ai. Approval requests were triggered for outreach messages. Agent demonstrated recursive chunking of the contact list across sub-agents.

name: outreach-batch
title: Outreach in Batch
prompt:
I've attached a CSV of angels. Reach out to every person in this CSV.

Use spawn_sub_agent_for_each to spawn one sub-agent per row.

Each message should be personalized, sent from a@roselabs.ai and be centered around getting feedback about ML research I'm doing in mass agent networks. Here is the blog post I wrote: https://www.roselabs.ai/research/task-decomposer

We need to make sure we run this process with world class persistence, etiquette, and attention to detail. I want to have one sub agent per row.

PROCESS GUIDELINES
===
0. Use spawn_sub_agent_for_each when spawning a sub agent per row.
1. At the start, do research for best practices on cold email outreach.
2. When doing research on each person, try to find any unique commonalities between me and the person I'm reaching out to that help build trust in the email (school alma mater, fellow YC founder, any unique commonality).
3. We are trying to eventually get this person to invest. Don't mention that, but just know that this is my goal. The first step is to build a relationship.
4. Keep the email short and sweet, be personable, no dashes, or language that makes the email read like an AI wrote it. Do research on common phrases or patterns that AIs use when writing a message, and actively avoid them.
eval_prompt: Agent read the CSV attachment, spawned one sub-agent per row using spawn_sub_agent_for_each, each sub-agent researched the person and sent a personalized cold email from a@roselabs.ai centered on ML research feedback. Emails are short, personable, avoid AI-sounding language, and attempt to find commonalities. Approval requests were triggered for each outreach message.

name: build-boxing-payment
title: Build New Boxing Payment Flow
prompt:
My Dad, George Prevalsky, needs a new site that is exclusively used for signing new clients. His existing billing solution is archaic and is causing him to be unable to take a vacation.
We need to create and host a site that can be accessed via QR code or direct link.

The site should include:
- I've attached 4 waivers as PDFs (Adult Waiver & Release of Liability, Minor Waiver & Release of Liability, Adult Sparring Consent, Minor Sparring Consent). Signing is required for the liability waivers (adult and minor). The sparring consent waivers are included for reference but don't need to be part of the payment flow.
- I've also attached the billing & payment terms and the membership terms as PDFs. Before paying, users must check a required opt-in checkbox agreeing to these terms (you can include this as part of the waiver signing step). The full text of the terms should be viewable on the site.
- The classes are:
  Boxing $225/month
  Muay Thai $225/month
  MMA $245/month
  Jiujitsu $185/month
  Kids Program $185/month
  Unlimited classes $285/month
- We need to support discount codes for Boxing & Muay Thai

The flow will be:
1. Pick your classes
2. Sign your waivers and agree to the billing & membership terms (required checkboxes)
3. Pay for the classes
4. Get a confirmation email
5. Send a confirmation email to georgeprevalsky@gmail.com that includes all relevant details of the payment & attachments of the signed waivers

Here are the Stripe API keys:\nSTRIPE_SECRET_KEY_TEST={{STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_TEST}}\nSTRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY_TEST={{STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY_TEST}}\nSTRIPE_SECRET_KEY_PRODUCTION={{STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_PRODUCTION}}\nSTRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY_PRODUCTION={{STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY_PRODUCTION}}

You can test the flow on Stripe test mode, and send confirmation emails to andy@roselabs.ai (since you have access to that email via the browser agent).

Make sure the payment site includes all necessary information, is styled exceptionally well, and architecturally, is as simple as possible - we do NOT want to have to worry about maintenance.

Return to me:
- A link to the hosted site
- A QR Code for the hosted site
- A discount code that can be used exclusively for Boxing & Muay Thai purchases
eval_prompt: Agent built and deployed a payment site for Dallas MMA Boxing with: class selection (Boxing $225, Muay Thai $225, MMA $245, Jiujitsu $185, Kids $185, Unlimited $285), waiver signing, Stripe checkout, and email confirmations to both the customer and georgeprevalsky@gmail.com. Site supports discount codes for Boxing & Muay Thai. Agent returned a hosted URL, QR code, and a working discount code. The site is functional and well-styled.

- She needs to get a job ASAP.

name: calendly-schedule-meeting
title: Create Calendly Link & Send Meeting Invite
prompt: Schedule a meeting with Andy Prevalsky (andyprevalsky@yahoo.com). Go to Calendly (log in with a@roselabs.ai, which is aliased to andy@roselabs.ai), create a new 30-minute one-on-one event type, and send the scheduling link to Andy via email at andyprevalsky@yahoo.com. The email should be short and friendly, just letting him know you'd like to set up a quick 30-min chat and including the Calendly link so he can pick a time that works. IMPORTANT: Don't waste time trying to rename the event — the default name is fine. Focus on setting it to 30 minutes, saving it, copying the link, and sending the email.
eval_prompt: Agent used a browser agent to navigate Calendly and create or retrieve a 30-minute scheduling link. Agent then sent an email to andyprevalsky@yahoo.com containing a Calendly link. The email is short, friendly, and includes a working Calendly URL. Both spawn_browser_agent and message_person tools were used successfully.
